text: The meeting identified the open problem of the UI's laptop failure (Windows hang) reducing the time available to complete tasks.

A combined power system with a rechargeable battery and kinetic energy as a back-up will be adopted, with the battery charged when the remote is moved, and the remote will use a square LCD as the standard touchscreen with an advanced LCD option if LCD is used.
The touchscreen concept will be housed in a protective case to prevent breakage, the casing must be firm and not bendable, and the remote will use rubber casing material.

Parental control will be incorporated but kept simple as a menu option; budget constraints may force moving from advanced chip sets to simpler button solutions if costs are not manageable, and using a combination battery and kinetic charging may increase costs.
Actions include taking notes and placing the minutes in the shared folder, creating a dynamic PowerPoint mock-up of the interface, and drawing the concept in 3-D.
